question.prompt: One ticket to a show costs \(\$20\) at full price. Susan buys \(4\) tickets using a coupon that gives her a \(25\%\) discount. Pam buys \(5\) tickets using a coupon that gives her a \(30\%\) discount. How many more dollars does Pam pay than Susan?

solutions.explanation:
A \(25\%\) discount means Susan pays \(75\%\) of the full price, while a \(30\%\) discount means Pam pays \(70\%\).

Susan's four tickets cost \(4\cdot20=80\) dollars before the discount, so she pays
\[
80\cdot0.75=60\text{ dollars}.
\]
Pam's five tickets cost \(5\cdot20=100\) dollars before the discount, so she pays
\[
100\cdot0.70=70\text{ dollars}.
\]
Pam pays \(70-60=\boxed{10}\) more dollars, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
